text:
matt: quick note — noticed steady memory growth on long convo workloads yesterday, looks like KV cache fragmentation. attaching short profile and heapdump snippet. :frowning_face:
anya: ugh ok, how steady? periodic spikes or linear drift?
lee: saw similar in perf test last week when we pushed the 4k max-context patch. linear-ish, esp after many small writes.
sophia: can you drop the profile here?
matt: pasted minimal output below:
```
# perf summary (kv cache alloc path)
rss_start=6.1G
rss_end=7.4G
delta=1.3G over 45m
kv_free_slots=12 (target 1024)
bucket_histogram: 32:120k, 64:48k, 128:9k, 256:1.2k
avg_alloc_size=74 bytes
frag_ratio=0.42
compaction_runs=0
```
matt: also saw a LOT of small slab residues around 32/64 buckets when we sampled the heap.
jamal: interesting — avg_alloc_size 74 bytes means a lot of tiny kv entries. buddy-style freelist will fragment badly.
anya: what about reuse? are we seeing high churn that prevents coalescing?
lee: replayed a trace locally: churn high, but many evictions leave odd-sized holes because we pin some slots for long-context caches (kv entries with long TTL).
sophia: two axes to consider: change block size mix (smaller microblocks for tiny entries) vs add a background micro-compactor that merges holes periodically. both have tradeoffs.
matt: yeah. my quick thoughts: 1) tune allocator bucket sizes to match measured alloc distribution (add 64->48 split?) 2) opportunistic compaction on eviction when free_frag_ratio > 0.3 3) track free-slot age and prefer reusing older holes for same-size requests to reduce scattering.
jamal: about kernel selection impact — if we introduce a compaction thread it will contend on GPU/CPU scheduling only if we run it during hot generation. maybe limit compaction to low-latency windows or offload to background workers on host CPU.
lee: also worth noting that batching heuristics amplify the problem: bigger batches increase KV cache locality but also extend the lifetime of more entries, raising long-tail pinning. we saw latency SLOs change when moving from 8->32 batch sizes.
anya: can we simulate a conservative tweak: add an extra 32-byte bucket and a microcompact pass that runs every 5m but stops if tail latency > target? cheap canary.
sophia: agree to test. hypothesis: small bucket reduces per-entry waste (avg waste -> -10-15%) and microcompact should reduce frag_ratio but may increase background CPU by ~2-4%.
matt: proposed experiment plan:
- variant A: add 32b bucket + allocator histogram adjustments
- variant B: existing + background microcompactor (5m cadence, stop-on-tl-violation)
- metrics: rss_growth_per_hour, frag_ratio, p99 latency, compactor_cpu, eviction_rate
- run on canary pool for 48h
jamal: I'll own A/B infra and dashboards. tagging @infra-bot to schedule canary.
infra-bot: canary cluster alloc request created: canary-kv-frag-5481234567, start=in 10m, duration=48h. ticket=INF-3421
lee: quick note — when you run A/B please also capture per-bucket free-age histogram. that will tell us if the age-based reuse is feasible.
anya: add a cheap probe that forces free-slot reuse for a tiny % of requests to validate reuse heuristics without full rollout.
sophia: also let's add a kernel-level metric: compaction latency per op and how it bumps tail. we should be conservative.
matt: cool. jamal, can you post the canary link + query ids when ready? i'll attach the small heap snapshot and follow up if we need a more aggressive compaction (full copy-compact).
jamal: will do. starting infra job now. :thumbsup: 
anya: thanks everyone — relieved we have a plan.
lee: fwiw, if compaction works we should document guidelines for batch sizing vs kv allocator profiles in the runtime tuning doc.
sophia: agreed — postmortem + runbook if we flip a flag in prod.
matt: updated notes pinned to thread. will follow up with snapshots once canary completes.
